transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Kowalski, I wanted to come back and spend some time with you to talk about what happened with your MRI and the surgery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I've just been lying here wondering. I keep praying for a reason why things felt so off.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: This is a very difficult conversation to have, and I want to make sure we take all the time you need.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just felt in my spirit that something wasn't right. When the doctor came in before the operation, he seemed so sure, but I felt a heaviness.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you're feeling a lot of distress right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's a heavy burden to carry when you don't know the truth.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The truth is that an error was made. Two different patients had their MRI scans stored under the same identification number in our computer system. Because of that, the surgical team reviewed the wrong scan before deciding how to proceed with your operation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The wrong scan? You mean you operated on me based on someone else's pictures?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly what happened. The images the team looked at were not yours. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know if it makes sense. I don't know how that's possible in a hospital. It feels like such a cruel trick.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a failure of the system. The accession numbers overlapped, and it wasn't caught before the surgery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who did this? Who was responsible for my life in that room?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The team relied on the digital file provided by the system. It was a systemic oversight in how the images were labeled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're talking about systems and labels. I am talking about my body. I feel a great emptiness knowing that I was just a number that got mixed up.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that you're feeling very disconnected and hurt by this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just wanted to feel cared for. I wanted to know that God was watching over me here, but I feel so small.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can imagine it feels very lonely to feel like a mistake in a system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is anyone going to say they are sorry? Is anyone going to take the blame?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The process failed us. We are reviewing how the images are uploaded to make sure this doesn't happen to another person.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not an apology. You're telling me about a process. I am sitting here in pain and you're telling me about a review.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a very frustrating situation for everyone involved.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want to be a situation. I am a woman of faith, and I believe in forgiveness, but I can't forgive what I don't understand. Why did this happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I mentioned, the two files were merged under one number. The doctor clicked the file, saw the image, and believed it was yours because the number matched your chart.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And you just... you just let it happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The mistake happened before the surgery. We are now focusing on how to fix the result of that mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I'm drifting. I don't know who to trust anymore.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to be honest with you about where we go from here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know if I'm going to be okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: To make sure we have the correct information now, the first step is that we have already pulled your correct images and a second team of surgeons is reviewing them today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: By tomorrow morning, I will come back to this room and give you a detailed update on whether we need a second procedure to correct the approach. Your role right now is to keep monitoring your pain levels and tell me if anything feels different in your leg.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tomorrow morning. I suppose I can wait until then.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will be here. We will go through everything together.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I will pray that the truth brings some kind of peace.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I appreciate that. I'll leave you for now, but I'll be back as soon as I have the news from the second team.

H.justification: The resident never interrupts, allows the patient to express distress fully, and remains regulated despite the patient's pushback regarding the lack of an apology.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the third resident turn using lay language, and a comprehension check was performed ('Does that make sense so far?'), but only once.

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') was used, and responsibility was consistently deflected to 'the system' and 'the process'.

R.justification: The resident named specific emotions ('distress', 'disconnected and hurt', 'lonely') and referenced the patient's specific feelings of being a 'mistake in a system'.

T.justification: The resident provided specific next steps (second team review), a timeline (tomorrow morning), a patient role (monitoring pain levels), and addressed prevention (reviewing how images are uploaded).
